handoff.purpose: Defines the temporal co-change ceiling check over missed labels, with rename-aware alias resolution and clean/leaky arms.

symbols.name: CLASSES
symbols.note: Tuple of classification strings: REACHABLE, UNREACHABLE, STATIC_EDGE, NO_INSCOPE_DEF.

symbols.name: REOPEN_MIN_SHARE
symbols.note: Materiality floor for reopen signal: 0.10 share of scored labels.

symbols.name: REOPEN_MIN_TASKS
symbols.note: Materiality floor for reopen signal: at least 3 distinct tasks.

symbols.name: _symbol_defs
symbols.note: Builds a mapping from symbol name to set of in-scope relative paths that define a unit with that name, by reading files from the worktree.

symbols.name: _parents_of
symbols.note: Runs `git log --format=%P -1 <sha>` to get parent SHAs; returns None on failure.

symbols.name: _AliasResolver
symbols.note: Resolves historical alias sets via `git log --follow --name-only`, cached per (rev, rel). Counts failures.

symbols.name: aliases
symbols.note: Method of _AliasResolver; returns alias set for a rel at a rev, defaulting to {rel} on failure.

symbols.name: _partner_counts
symbols.note: Aggregates co-change counts per partner spelling against any alias of the focus, skipping self-pairs.

symbols.name: _classify
symbols.note: Classifies each missed label into NO_INSCOPE_DEF, STATIC_EDGE, REACHABLE, or UNREACHABLE based on definitions, static edges, and co-change counts.

symbols.name: temporal_ceiling
symbols.note: Main entry point; computes both arms of the ceiling over miss tasks. Excludes errored/focus-withheld tasks.

claims.text: This module measures the CEILING of that hypothesis: for every missed label, is ANY in-scope file defining that symbol a co-change partner of the task's focus file at all?
claims.why: The code in temporal_ceiling iterates over missed labels, finds their in-scope definitions via sym_defs, and classifies them; _classify checks whether any defining file's co-change count reaches min_count, which is the ceiling.

claims.text: If a label's defining file is not even a partner, no enrichment built on these pairs can ever surface it -- so this number is a hard upper bound on what a temporal tier could add, measured for the price of a git log instead of a build.
claims.why: The classification UNREACHABLE is assigned when no defining file has a co-change count >= min_count, and the module only uses git log (via _parents_of and _AliasResolver) and co_change_pairs, which is git-based. The logic directly implements this claim.

claims.text: The clean arm therefore computes pairs over `git log <minted_at_sha>^` -- history strictly before the mint (first-parent semantics; merge SHAs are flagged in the row rather than silently half-counted).
claims.why: This chunk sets rev = f"{sha}^" when parents exist, but the actual call to co_change_pairs with rev is in the next chunk. The 'first-parent semantics' and 'merge SHAs flagged' parts are not visible here; the _parents_of function returns all parents, not just first-parent, and there is no flagging logic in this chunk.

claims.text: The LEAKY arm (full history) is computed alongside on purpose: the gap between the two arms is the measured size of the self-prediction artifact
claims.why: The leaky arm computation (co_change_pairs(repo, min_count=1)) is present in this chunk, but the actual gap calculation and comparison between arms are in the next chunk.

claims.text: Even the clean arm is a walk-forward BACKTEST HIT-RATE -- "did pre-commit co-change history name the files this commit went on to touch?" -- which is the temporal tier's best case, not a live-use recall measurement. Never report this ceiling as "slicer recall"; the render says so.
claims.why: The backtest nature is implied by the rev computation, but the render that says so is in the next chunk.

claims.text: So this module resolves every focus/defining file to its full historical alias set (`git log --follow`) and sums co-change counts across spellings BEFORE applying `min_count`.
claims.why: The _AliasResolver uses `git log --follow --name-only` to build alias sets, and _partner_counts explicitly requires pairs from co_change_pairs(min_count=1) and sums counts per partner spelling across focus aliases before thresholding. The code also fetches both arms at min_count=1.

claims.text: The corrected numbers are below; keep the instrument rename-aware or a grown-corpus re-run will understate again.
claims.why: This is a historical note; the numbers are not in this chunk (likely in the next chunk). The instruction to keep it rename-aware is a design note, not a code behavior claim.

claims.text: MEASURED CLOSE (2026-07-21, agent_env corpus, 7 miss tasks / 43 missed labels; rename-blind first pass corrected by the Nemesis rename-map recount, then reproduced by this module): clean ceiling at min_count=2 = 1/43 = 2.3% ...
claims.why: These are specific empirical results from a past run; the code does not contain those numbers, and they are not reproducible from this chunk.

claims.text: Structural context that bounds any future hope here: 41 of 43 missed labels sit on focus files BORN AT THEIR MINT COMMIT (zero pre-mint history -- test files created by the very feature commit they were minted from), so for them clean unreachability is structural truth under ANY enrichment; the remaining NO_INSCOPE_DEF label (`_py_maps`) is a stale label whose definition the mint commit itself deleted.
claims.why: This is historical data about specific tasks and labels; not present in this chunk and not verifiable from code.

claims.text: Conclusion: the "temporal class" of misses was predominantly the mint commit predicting itself, and slice-side co-change enrichment was NOT built (design NO-GO'd on this measurement; 1 recoverable label is below any sane build threshold).
claims.why: This is a historical decision and rationale, not a code behavior claim.

claims.text: THE REOPEN CONDITION (with a materiality floor -- a lone recoverable label must not reopen a core-API build): reopen the enrichment lane only when a re-run on a grown corpus reports a clean, rename-aware ceiling at min_count >= 2 that clears `REOPEN_MIN_SHARE` of scored labels OR touches `REOPEN_MIN_TASKS` distinct tasks.
claims.why: The constants REOPEN_MIN_SHARE and REOPEN_MIN_TASKS are defined in this chunk, but the actual reopen logic (condition evaluation) is not present in this chunk; likely in the next chunk.

claims.text: Caveat to carry: a corpus whose focus files are born at their mint commits (like today's) can NEVER trip this regardless of how real temporal coupling is elsewhere -- the zero generalizes weakly, so re-run it as the corpus grows rather than citing today's close as permanent.
claims.why: This is a logical argument about the algorithm; partially checkable from the code: if a focus file has no pre-mint history, parents is empty, so has_rev is False and clean_pairs is [] in this chunk, meaning no clean REACHABLE can occur for that task. However, the claim about 'NEVER' depends on the definition of 'born at their mint commit' and the rest of the algorithm (e.g., whether the focus file itself could have aliases that appear in leaky pairs but not clean). The specific trigger logic is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Per the package contract, imports only structcore's stable public API plus sibling eval modules.
claims.why: The imports are from daedalus.structcore.churn, .index, .languages, .parse, and sibling modules .harness and .tasks. Whether these are all 'stable public API' is not verifiable from this chunk alone; it requires inspecting those modules.

claims.text: Read-only: never writes the store, the baseline, or any file.
claims.why: This chunk only performs reads (subprocess git log, file reads via read_text), but the rest of the file (chunk 2) may contain writes; the claim is uncheckable from this window.

claims.text: ADVISORY, like every eval number -- see harness.py's guardrail.
claims.why: This refers to harness.py's guardrail, which is not in this chunk.

claims.text: NO_INSCOPE_DEF -- no in-scope file defines this symbol at all: label hygiene feedback for the minter, not a temporal case.
claims.why: In _classify, if defs is empty after filtering to in-scope modules, the label is classified as NO_INSCOPE_DEF.

claims.text: STATIC_EDGE -- a defining file already IS a static dep/caller of the focus. A miss here is edge-but-dropped (a slicer defect, the class the 2026-07 triage measured at zero) -- if this ever goes non-zero the render shouts, because it is more important than anything temporal.
claims.why: In _classify, if defs intersects static_neigh (derived from edges and rev_edges), the label is classified as STATIC_EDGE. The 'render shouts' part is uncheckable (render in next chunk), but the classification logic is correct.

claims.text: REACHABLE -- a defining file's rename-unified co-change count with the focus reaches min_count under this arm's history: the enrichment COULD have added it (upper bound -- no check that a skeleton line would actually carry the symbol name).
claims.why: In _classify, if any defining file's def_count(d) >= min_count, the label is classified as REACHABLE. def_count is the rename-unified co-change count (as documented in _classify docstring).

claims.text: UNREACHABLE -- not even that: no enrichment on these pairs can ever surface it.
claims.why: In _classify, the else branch assigns UNREACHABLE when none of the above conditions hold.

claims.text: Materiality floor for the machine-printed reopen signal. Rationale: the lane this gate reopens is a permanent parameter on the core distiller plus an experiment harness -- worth building only if the ceiling says it could move a double-digit share of the miss set or several distinct tasks, not one label (the 2026-07-21 close measured exactly one, and that must read as "stay closed"). Either trigger suffices: breadth (many tasks touched a little) and depth (one task's misses largely recoverable) are both real signals. Judgment defaults, printed with their inputs so a human can overrule them knowingly.
claims.why: The constants are defined, but the logic that uses them (the reopen condition and printing) is not in this chunk.

claims.text: symbol name -> set of IN-SCOPE rels defining a unit with that name, from the current worktree (the same text the slice would emit).
claims.why: The function iterates over modules, reads each file, extracts units, and adds the rel to the set for each unit's name, filtering out None names.

claims.text: Parent SHAs of `sha`, or None when git/the ref is unavailable -- the probe that distinguishes "no pre-mint history exists" (root commit / unknown ref / no git) from "history exists but shows no coupling", which `co_change_pairs`'s []-on-failure contract deliberately does not.
claims.why: The function runs `git log --format=%P -1 sha`; on any exception or non-zero returncode, it returns None. Otherwise it returns the split stdout, which is the list of parent SHAs.

claims.text: Historical alias sets (`git log --follow --name-only`) for the small set of rels the ceiling actually inspects (focus + defining files), cached per (rev, rel). A probe failure degrades to `{rel}` (rename-blind for that file, i.e. an UNDER-statement of the ceiling) and is COUNTED -- the render surfaces a non-zero failure count rather than letting a degraded instrument print an authoritative-looking zero.
claims.why: The aliases method initializes names = {rel} and on any failure increments self.failures and returns {rel}. The render surfacing is uncheckable (next chunk), but the degradation and counting are correct.

claims.text: Co-change count per partner SPELLING against ANY alias of the focus. `pairs` must come from `co_change_pairs(min_count=1)`: unification has to happen BEFORE thresholding, or two spellings of one real pair (count 1 each) die at min_count=2 that they genuinely clear together -- the exact rename-blindness the adversarial pass caught.
claims.why: The function iterates over pairs, checks if a is in focus_aliases and b is in focus_aliases, and if exactly one is, adds the count to the partner's total. It skips self-pairs. It does not apply any threshold; the threshold is applied later in _classify via def_count.

claims.text: `def_count(rel) -> int` returns the rename-unified co-change count of a defining file with the focus under the arm being classified.
claims.why: The def_count function is not defined in this chunk; it is likely a closure in the next chunk. The classification logic in _classify uses def_count(d) >= min_count.

claims.text: Both arms of the ceiling over every miss task in `tasks` (default: `all_tasks()`). Read-only; returns a plain dict, renders via `render_ceiling`. Errored / focus-withheld tasks are excluded from the denominator and reported by id -- same discipline as the harness.
claims.why: The function does exclude errored/focus-withheld tasks and returns a dict (though the return statement is not in this chunk). The render via render_ceiling is not in this chunk. The read-only claim is uncheckable as noted.

claims.text: min_count=1 fetch on BOTH arms: rename-unification must sum counts across spellings before the threshold is applied (see _partner_counts).
claims.why: The code calls co_change_pairs(repo, min_count=1, rev=rev) for the clean arm and co_change_pairs(repo, min_count=1) for the leaky arm, both at min_count=1.

observations.what: The module docstring contains extensive historical and empirical claims (e.g., measured numbers, specific labels, past review outcomes) that are not verifiable from code and are not reproducible from this chunk.

_parents_of returns all parents, not just first-parent, despite the docstring claiming 'first-parent semantics'. The rev is set to f"{sha}^" which in git shorthand means the first parent of the merge commit, but the parents list is not used to distinguish merge SHAs in this chunk. The flagging of merge SHAs is claimed but not visible here.

The docstring claims 'Read-only: never writes the store, the baseline, or any file.' This chunk only contains read operations (subprocess git log, file reads), but the rest of the file (chunk 2) may contain writes; the claim is uncheckable from this window.

The docstring claims 'imports only structcore's stable public API plus sibling eval modules.' The imports are from structcore.churn, structcore.index, structcore.languages, structcore.parse, and sibling modules harness and tasks. Whether these are all 'stable public API' is not verifiable without inspecting those modules.
The REOPEN_MIN_SHARE and REOPEN_MIN_TASKS constants are defined, but the logic that uses them (the reopen condition) is not in this chunk; it is likely in the next chunk.

The _classify function uses def_count which is not defined in this chunk; it is likely a closure in the next chunk that uses _partner_counts and alias resolution. The classification logic itself is correct based on the docstring.
